stats.fact: Anthropic's official Claude Code docs describe skills as SKILL.md-based extensions that load on demand, unlike CLAUDE.md content that enters the context at startup.
Claude Code bundled skills include /code-review, /batch, /debug, /loop, and /claude-api, with /run, /verify, and /run-skill-generator available for running and verifying apps in current docs.

Anthropic's extension overview says teams commonly add features in this order: CLAUDE.md for repeated convention misses, skills for repeated prompts or playbooks, MCP for copied external data, code-intelligence plugins for symbol navigation, subagents for noisy side tasks, hooks for automatic actions, and plugins for reuse across repositories.
Official Claude Code docs define plugins as the packaging layer that can bundle skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers into one installable unit.

Claude Code's MCP docs say Claude Code can connect to hundreds of external tools and data sources through MCP, and recommends connecting a server when users are copying data from systems such as issue trackers or monitoring dashboards into chat.

Anthropic reported on December 9, 2025 that MCP had more than 10,000 active public servers, adoption by ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Visual Studio Code, and other AI products, and 97M+ monthly SDK downloads across Python and TypeScript.
The official MCP project blog also reported on December 9, 2025 that MCP had over 97 million monthly SDK downloads, 10,000 active servers, and first-class client support across major AI platforms.
The official MCP Registry launched in preview on September 8, 2025 as an open catalog and API for discovering publicly available MCP servers and a primary source of truth for downstream registries.

A May 24, 2026 MCP adoption statistics review counted 9,652 latest records and 28,959 server/version records from the official MCP Registry API, while noting that registry records do not count private enterprise servers or every downstream marketplace entry.

angles: Lead with a decision framework: install fewer things, but choose the right layer for the job: skill, MCP, hook, subagent, plugin, or CLAUDE.md.

Rank a lean team stack rather than every shiny community tool: project rules, code review, docs fetch, browser/web research, test runner, UI/design, security, issue tracker, database, and observability.
Make the key distinction clear: skills teach Claude how your team works; MCP servers give Claude access to external systems; plugins package the setup for reuse.
Unique insight: the best 2026 stack is not skills versus MCP. It is skills plus MCP plus deterministic hooks, with plugins used only after the setup proves repeatable across repos.
Security angle: MCP servers and skill scripts can execute real actions or make network calls, so start read-only, audit scripts, use environment variables, and prefer official vendor servers.
Team workflow angle: keep personal experimentation in user-level skills, commit stable project skills under .claude/skills, and package cross-repo standards as plugins.
Context hygiene angle: use subagents for noisy investigation and research, skills for reusable procedures, and hooks for rules that should not rely on model compliance.
Bloat angle: a mature Claude Code setup should include pruning and auditing, because unused skills and too many MCP tools can hurt routing, latency, and trust.
Governance angle: as MCP registries and gateways mature, teams should treat agent-to-tool access like API access, with inventory, ownership, permissions, and review cadence.
